description: The P0 shell plus task #37's opener grant. build.rs declares an app ACL manifest (ADR-0012) naming every command in generate_handler! (six at P0, sixteen with the P1 set), so this file's grant is now enforcement, not documentation: it names the commands the front end actually has a wrapper for (a client.ts function, not necessarily a UI caller yet): the five P0 ones -- authored in app/src/ipc/client.ts and shipped as the Vite output crates/serat-app/webview/boot.js, which since task #98 is generated rather than hand-written (F-467) -- read_file, write_file, index_status, mark_first_paint, mark_vault_usable. open_vault is deliberately withheld; nothing in the webview calls it (F-342), it is invoked only from Rust inside setup, and granting it here would reopen surface removing it was meant to close. Task #18 (P1) adds ten more, each granted on purpose to main and pinned in security_config.rs and acl_manifest.rs: refused_names, create_folder, search, backlinks, get_ui_settings, set_live_preview, set_keybinding, and the three ignore-offer commands (append_gitignore_entry is the single named T-06 exception and takes no path). Task #18c adds eight more: switcher_query (the quick switcher, architecture 9.2), open_tree, mark_tree, note_opened, note_closed, save_patch, request_external_diff, rebase_buffer (the tree stream and the editor buffers, ADR-0015/0016). Widening this set is a threat-model decision, not a convenience -- see docs/03-design/adr/0012-declare-the-tauri-app-acl-manifest.md. `opener:allow-open-url` is scoped here to exactly http/https/mailto (§9.3, T-09) -- narrower than tauri-plugin-opener's own `default` permission set, which also grants `tel:` and reveal-in-file-explorer; neither is used and both stay ungranted.
